body:
These days, AI-based programs or robots are widely used in the (A)[medical / travel] industry. Some AI programs ⓐhave been refined to the point that they can not only identify cancer quickly and accurately, but also ⓑpredicting the chance of getting cancer. AI robots are also used in operating rooms. ⓒBased on the collected data, AI surgical robots can conduct (B)[cognitive / physical] activities such as voice recognition, decision-making, problem-solving, and more. Under the guidance and control of doctors, they can conduct (C)[elementary / autonomous] operations such as cutting and stitching patients undergoing surgery. ⓓAnother example is the development of an AI system to forecast when a hospitalized patient’s condition is likely to get worse. It analyzes the patient’s profile and data and ⓔassigns scores indicating the need for transfer to an intensive care unit. The medical team intervenes when a patient’s scores reach a certain level.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: medical cognitive autonomous
travel cognitive autonomous
medical cognitive elementary
travel physical elementary
medical physical elementary
solution:
(A) 암을 진단하거나 발병 확률을 예측하는 AI 프로그램, AI 수술 로봇 등이 사용되는 예가 이어서 소개되므로, AI 기반 프로그램이나 로봇이 의료 산업에서 널리 사용되고 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 medical(의료의, 의학의)이 알맞다.
travel 여행, 관광
(B) 음성 인식, 의사 결정, 문제 해결 등이 AI 활동의 예로 제시되므로, AI 수술 로봇이 인지 활동을 수행할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 cognitive(인지적인)가 알맞다.
physical 신체적인
(C) 의사의 지도와 통제 아래 이루어진다고 언급했으며, 예시로 절개나 봉합이 제시되므로, AI 수술 로봇이 수술 중인 환자에게 기본적인 수술을 수행할 수 있다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 elementary(기본적인, 기초적인)가 알맞다.
autonomous 자율적인

body:
The film production industry extensively utilizes AI in various ways. This is because it not only assists producers in creating films more conveniently, but also enables them to make what they intended to express come alive with enhanced realism and naturalness. Recently, an AI-based program was developed, through which actors’ faces on the screen are aged or made younger. For example, when provided with the input of a thirty-five-year-old man’s face, the AI program generates different facial images at different ages. While there have been existing techniques that can achieve similar results, they required an extensive process. However, the newly developed automatic program accelerates the process. In order to develop this program, thousands of pictures of faces ranging from eighteen years old to eighty-five years old were accumulated as input to this program. It was then trained to learn how faces change as people age, and derived the principles for aging. With them, the program can manipulate the facial changes of actors with the addition or removal of wrinkles. As a result, it can produce output that is highly realistic. These results are maintained even when the actors make varied facial expressions. Due to the convenience and the naturalness of the results, it is expected that this technique will be widely incorporated in filmmaking.
윗글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: the history of makeup techniques in the film industry
the limitations of using AI programs in movie production
the process of casting actors for different age groups in films
the ethical concerns over altering actors’ appearances with AI
how AI makes filmmaking more convenient and its results more realistic
solution:
영화 제작 산업은 AI가 제작자들이 영화를 더 편리하게 만들도록 도울 뿐만 아니라 그들이 표현하고자 한 것을 더 사실적이고 자연스럽게 구현하게 해 주기 때문에 AI를 다양하게 활용한다고 한 뒤, 그 예로 배우의 얼굴을 나이 들게 하거나 젊게 만드는 AI 프로그램이 과정을 빠르게 하고 매우 사실적인 결과를 만들어 낸다고 설명하고 있으므로, 글의 주제로 ⑤ ‘AI가 어떻게 영화 제작을 더 편리하게 하고 그 결과물을 더 사실적으로 만드는지’가 알맞다.
오답
① 영화 산업에서 분장 기법의 역사
② 영화 제작에서 AI 프로그램을 사용하는 것의 한계
③ 영화에서 서로 다른 연령대를 위한 배우를 캐스팅하는 과정
④ AI로 배우들의 외모를 바꾸는 것에 대한 윤리적 우려들

body:
Several artificial intelligence (AI) technologies described in films are now a reality. One of them is self-driving cars. driven directly by a human pilot inside the vehicle
unable to function properly without manual operation

body:
AI has been progressing rapidly over the years, and its potential is only beginning to be fully recognized. It is certain that AI will continue to play a significant role in more and more aspects of our lives. Accordingly, these days, a lot of movies feature various kinds of AI. Some AI robots have personalities and emotionally engage with people in the same way that humans do. Furthermore, some AI characters are physically indistinguishable from humans. These movies are not only fun to watch, but also inspiring. They show us what AI might be like in the future and how it could affect us. What AI technology from a movie do you think will be used in our lives in the future?
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: The full potential of AI is only now starting to be acknowledged.
There is no doubt that AI will keep playing an important part in increasingly diverse areas of our lives.
A wide range of films nowadays showcase different types of AI technologies.
In films, some AI entities possess distinct personalities and build emotional connections with people.
Some AI characters in films are easily distinguished from humans by their appearance.
solution:
일부 AI 캐릭터는 신체적으로 인간과 구분이 안 된다고 했으므로, ⑤ ‘영화 속 일부 AI 캐릭터들은 외모로 인간과 쉽게 구별된다.’는 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는다.
오답
① AI의 완전한 잠재력은 이제 막 인정되기 시작하고 있다.
② AI가 우리 삶의 점점 더 다양한 영역에서 중요한 역할을 계속할 것이라는 데는 의심의 여지가 없다.
③ 오늘날 다양한 영화들이 서로 다른 종류의 AI 기술을 보여 준다.
④ 영화에서, 일부 AI 존재들은 뚜렷한 개성을 지니고 사람들과 정서적 유대를 형성한다.

body:
In 2015, Matthew McConaughey, an American actor and producer, gave the (A)commencement speech at the University of Houston. Speaking to some 4,000 graduates, he shared personal stories and lessons, ⓐhoping to help young people find their paths in life.
Today, I’m going to talk to you about some things I’ve learned in life. I hope you think of them as (B)signposts or approaches that can guide your paths in life. You can apply them in your own lives, in your own ways if you ⓑchoose to. So here we go.
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. ㉠______, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of (C)standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. ㉡______, if happiness is ⓒthat you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. ㉢______, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do ⓓwhat we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a (D)means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally ⓔbecame happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own (E)reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ that → what (전치사 after의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(you’re after)을 이끌어, is의 보어 역할을 하는 명사절을 이루어야 하므로, 완전한 절을 이끄는 명사절 접속사 that을 선행사를 포함해 ‘~한 것’이라는 의미로 명사절을 이끄는 관계대명사 what으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ choose는 to부정사를 목적어로 취할 수 있으며, 동사(구)의 반복을 피하기 위해 to부정사에서 to만 남기고 나머지를 생략한 형태인 대부정사를 쓸 수 있으므로, choose와 to부정사의 to 뒤에 동사원형 apply를 포함한 동사구 ‘apply them in your own lives, in your own ways’가 생략된 choose to는 알맞다.
ⓔ 흐름상 주어 I에 대한 첫 번째 과거동사 began과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬연결을 이루어야 하며, 뒤에 보어인 비교급 형태의 형용사 happier가 있으므로, 2형식 동사 become의 과거형인 became은 알맞다.

This kind of (C)standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. ㉡______, if happiness is ⓒthat you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. ㉢______, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do ⓓwhat we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a (D)means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally ⓔbecame happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own (E)reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: McConaughey urges listeners to pursue joy over happiness.
In McConaughey's example, winning brings happiness while losing does not.
Joy is presented as a feeling that comes in response to a particular result.
McConaughey once concentrated on results, wanting his films to succeed commercially and his acting to be recognized.
McConaughey reminds listeners that joy is something they are continually creating.

Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to ⓐfinding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. (A)저는 거기에 없었어야 했고, Wooderson도 그러지 말아야 했습니다. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we ⓑdo.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually (B)[realizing / ignoring] who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not ⓒhelp us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or ⓓengaging in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and (C)[keep / stop] giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are (D)[healthier / unhealthier] for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things ⓔleaving in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞은 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓐ 명사 step 뒤에 전치사 to가 와서 ‘step to+명사(구)/동명사(구)(~로의 단계)’의 형태로 쓰일 수 있으며, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 our identity가 있으므로, 목적어를 취할 수 있는 동명사 finding은 알맞다.
ⓑ 일반동사(구)의 반복을 피하기 위해 대동사 do/does/did를 쓸 수 있으므로, 흐름상 현재형 복수동사 belong을 대신하는 대동사 do는 알맞다.
오답
ⓒ help → helps (동명사구 주어인 ‘Defining ourselves by who we are not’에 대한 동사가 올 자리이며, 동명사(구)는 단수 취급하므로, 수일치를 위해 복수동사 help를 단수동사 helps로 고친다.)
ⓓ engaging → engage (조동사 may 뒤에 두 개의 동사원형이 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결된 형태의 동사구 bully and gossip과 등위접속사 or에 의해 병렬연결을 이루어야 하므로, engaging을 동사원형 engage로 고친다.)
ⓔ leaving → left (동사 have와 목적어인 명사구 important things 뒤에 앞의 명사구를 수식하는 분사구를 이끄는 분사가 올 수 있으나, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘남겨진’ 대상이고 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 leaving을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 left로 고친다.)

Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves ⓐ[overcoming / to overcome] that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and (A)______. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, ⓑ[abandoning / abandoned] your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined ⓒ[having / to have] to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are (B)the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ ⓑ ⓒ
choices: overcoming abandoned having
overcoming abandoning to have
to overcome abandoned to have
to overcome abandoning to have
to overcome abandoning having
solution:
ⓐ ‘~을 부추겨서 …하게 하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘dare+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하므로, 동사 dare와 목적어인 ourselves 뒤에 to부정사인 to overcome이 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘Don’t+동사원형 ~‘ 형태인 부정 명령문 ‘don’t deny that they exist’ 뒤에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 연결되어 있으므로 분사구문을 이루는 분사 자리이며, 명령문의 생략된 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 you가 ‘포기하는’ 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 your opportunity 이하의 명사구가 이어지므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 abandoning이 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘~할 운명이다, ~하게 되어 있다’라는 뜻으로 ‘be destined+to부정사(구)’를 사용하므로, 형용사 destined 뒤에 to부정사인 to have가 알맞다.

body:
Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. Whichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you to grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and exposes you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless you put it to use, particularly good use. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something much more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring that no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me to measure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: Education keeps people within the boundaries they are already familiar with.
As a child, Sotomayor had clearly pictured herself working at the Supreme Court.
According to Sotomayor, education becomes less valuable when it is not used well.
Sotomayor believes that improving one's community requires a highly visible role like a Supreme Court justice.
Sotomayor's family taught her to judge happiness by her career achievements.
solution:
교육의 가치는 그것을 활용하지 않으면, 특히 바람직한 활용이 아니면 줄어든다고 했으므로, ③ 'Sotomayor에 따르면, 교육은 잘 사용되지 않을 때 덜 가치 있게 된다.'는 일치하는 내용이다.
오답
① 교육은 사람들을 그들이 이미 익숙한 경계 안에 머무르게 한다. (→교육은 여러분이 한때 알았던 한계를 넘어 성장할 수 있도록 힘을 실어주고, 여러분이 이미 알고 있는 곳과 사고방식 너머로 여러분을 이끈다.)
② 어렸을 때, Sotomayor는 자신이 대법원에서 일하는 모습을 분명히 그렸다. (→대법원은 어린 시절의 가장 대담한 꿈을 넘어서는 직장이었다.)
④ Sotomayor는 자신의 지역사회를 개선하는 것은 대법관과 같이 매우 눈에 띄는 역할을 필요로 한다고 생각한다. (→Sotomayor는 지역사회와 세상에 대한 개선은 대법관이 되는 것처럼 거창하거나 공개적인 방식일 필요는 없다고 말한다.)
⑤ Sotomayor의 가족은 그녀에게 자신의 직업적 성취로 행복을 판단하라고 가르쳤다. (→그녀의 가족은 자신이 직업으로서 무슨 일을 하는가가 아니라 다른 사람들에게 무엇을 베푸는가로 행복을 측정하라고 가르쳤다.)

body:
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
다음 글의 요지로 알맞은 것은?
choices: Career success is the most dependable source of lasting happiness.
Happiness and joy are similar in that both rely on achieving specific goals.
Enjoying our daily work is the surest way to achieve greater external success.
We should pursue joy in the process rather than happiness dependent on results.
We should keep raising our standards after reaching each goal to stay motivated.

행복은 결과에 대한 감정적 반응이며, 그것을 얻을 때마다 기준을 높이게 되어 지속할 수 없는 반면, 기쁨은 결과와 관계없이 우리가 해야 할 일을 할 때 경험하는 지속적인 감정이라고 한 뒤, 배우로서의 개인적 경험에 빗대어 결과와 상관없이 자신의 일을 즐기기 시작했을 때 이전보다 더 좋은 결과가 따랐고, 그러한 결과 외에도 기쁨이 늘 곁에 있었다는 것을 깨달았다고 말하고 있으므로, 글의 요지로 ④ ‘우리는 결과에 좌우되는 행복보다 과정 속의 기쁨을 추구해야 한다.'가 알맞다.
오답
① 직업적 성공은 지속적인 행복의 가장 믿을 만한 원천이다.
② 행복과 기쁨은 둘 다 특정한 목표를 이루는 것에 의존한다는 점에서 비슷하다.
③ 일상의 일을 즐기는 것은 더 큰 외적 성공을 이루는 가장 확실한 방법이다.
⑤ 우리는 동기를 유지하기 위해 각 목표에 도달한 후 기준을 계속 높여야 한다.

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Discovering our true self usually begins with (A)______ things that do not truly represent us, and (B)______ such things leaves us with only what really matters.
(A) (B)
choices: recognizing embracing
recognizing removing
ignoring embracing
hiding removing
ignoring analyzing

This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately (A)[raise / lower] the standard ⓓevery time we achieve it. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a(n) (B)[constant / inconstant] feeling ⓔthat we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the (C)[process / outcome], thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role (D)______, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. solution:
(A) 행복은 결과에 의존하는 감정적 반응이라고 한 뒤, 이러한 기준이 행복을 우리가 지속시킬 수 없는 것으로 만든다는 것의 이유로서 어떤 목표를 이룰 때마다 즉시 기준을 높인다는 흐름이 되어야 하므로, raise(~을 높이다)가 알맞다.
lower ~을 낮추다
(B) 지속시킬 수 없는 행복과 달리 기쁨은 구체적인 결과에 대한 반응이 아니라 결과와 관계없이 경험하는 감정이라고 한 뒤, 배우로서 자신의 경험을 이야기하며 결과 외에도 기쁨이 늘 곁에 있었다는 것을 깨달았다고 말하고 있으므로, 기쁨이 지속적인 감정이라고 설명하는 흐름이 되는 constant(끊임없이 계속되는, 지속적인)가 알맞다.
inconstant 쉽게 변하는, 일관성 없는
(C) 배우로서 과거에 가졌던 태도에 관해 말하고 있으며, 영화가 흥행에 성공해야 하고 자신의 연기가 인정받아야 한다고 생각했다는 내용이 이어지므로, 과정이 아닌 결과에 집중하는 태도였다는 흐름이 되는 outcome(결과)이 알맞다.
process 과정

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare ⓐmyself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. (A)저는 두려움이 자산이라고 생각하는데, 이것이 우리 스스로에게 그 두려움을 극복하도록 부추기는 필요성을 높이기 때문입니다. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear ⓑthat he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they ⓒare deserved. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity ⓓto overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and ⓔgive them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ are deserved → deserve (앞의 주어 they가 가리키는 fears가 타동사 deserve(~을 받을 만하다)의 주체이며, 명사구 the credit이 의미상 목적어에 해당하므로, they 이하는 앞에 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that이 생략된 채로 선행사인 the credit을 수식하는 관계사절이며, 능동태 타동사 deserve의 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절의 형태가 되어야 한다. 따라서 수동태 are deserved를 능동태 deserve로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ to부정사를 이루는 동사원형 scare의 목적어 자리이며, to부정사의 의미상 주어인 I와 동일한 대상이므로, 재귀 용법의 재귀대명사 myself는 알맞다.
ⓔ 동사원형으로 시작하는 앞의 명령문(confront your fears)과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 두 번째 명령문을 이끌어야 하므로, 동사원형 give는 알맞다.

body:
Born in 1954, Sonia Sotomayor is an American lawyer. She is the first Latin-American Supreme Court justice in US history.
For each of you, different courses and topics you study will help you navigate your lives in different ways. ⓐWhichever way these are for you, I know that they will help you on your journey, because education empowers you ⓑto grow beyond the limits you once knew, and it takes you beyond the places and ways of thinking you already know and ⓒexpose you to the greater potential that exists in the world. My education taught me about the Supreme Court, a workplace beyond my wildest dreams as a child. But the value of an education diminishes unless (A)______. Good use includes earning a living and supporting your families. But it also means something ⓓmuch more significant. It means contributing to the betterment of the community and world you live in. That betterment does not have to be in a big or public way like becoming a Supreme Court justice. My grandmother bettered her community by ensuring ⓔthat no one around her ever went hungry. My mom as a practical nurse would give shots to neighbors who needed them or help others with blood pressure readings or changing of bandages. Just as I am sure you have learned, my family taught me ⓕmeasure happiness not by what I do as work but by what I give to others. It is the most important lesson and the deepest source of meaning I have found in life.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓒ expose → exposes (노출시키는 주체가 주어 it이므로, 단수동사 takes가 이끄는 동사구 ‘takes ~ know’와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되는 동사구를 이끌도록 expose를 단수동사 exposes로 고친다.)
ⓕ measure → to measure (동사 teach는 ‘teach+목적어+목적격보어(~에게 …하도록 가르치다)’의 5형식 구문에서 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, taught와 목적어 me에 이어진 목적격보어 자리의 동사원형 measure를 to부정사인 to measure로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ ‘~에게 …할 권한을 부여하다’라는 뜻으로 ‘empower+목적어+to부정사(구)’를 사용하므로, empowers와 목적어 you 뒤에 이어진 to부정사 to grow는 알맞다.

body:
Number One. Seek joy, not happiness. What is happiness? Happiness is an emotional response to an outcome. Happiness demands a certain outcome. In other words, it depends on the outcome. If I win, I will be happy. If I don’t, I won’t. This kind of standard makes happiness something that we can’t sustain because we immediately raise the standard every time we achieve it. Therefore, if happiness is what you’re after, then you’re going to be disappointed frequently and be unhappy for much of your time. However, joy is a different thing. It’s not a reaction to a specific outcome. Joy is a constant feeling that we experience when we do what we are meant to do, regardless of the outcome.
Personally, as an actor, I used to have an attitude that focused on the outcome, thinking, “I need this film to be a box office success. I need my performance to be acknowledged.” However, when I stopped trying to make the daily labor a means to a certain end, I began to enjoy my work and literally became happier. As soon as the daily act of making a movie or performing a role became its own reward for me, I received more box office successes and more awards than I ever had before. However, what I realized was that aside from the results, joy was always with me. Remember that joy is always “in process” and we are always making it.
윗글의 두 번째 단락에 드러난 ‘I’의 태도 변화로 알맞은 것은?
choices: indifferent to success → hungry for fame
eager for recognition → obsessed with awards
confident in his talent → doubtful of his ability
fixated on results → absorbed in the work itself
engrossed in the task itself → focused on results

body:
Number two. The process of elimination is the first step to finding our identity. In 1992, I got my first job as an actor. Initially, I only had three lines, but the director suggested giving me more scenes and lines. I was thrilled and agreed to the offer because it meant more screen time and a higher income. However, a few years ago, when I watched the film again, I realized that there were two scenes where my character, Wooderson, didn’t fit in. I shouldn’t have been there, and neither should Wooderson. It is just as important to know where we don’t belong as it is to know where we do.
So, the first step that leads to our identity in life is usually realizing who we are not. Defining ourselves by who we are not helps us truly understand who we are. You know that some friends you hang out with really don’t bring out the best in you. They may bully and gossip too much or engage in questionable behavior. You know that they really aren’t going to be there for you when you’re in trouble. Now, be assertive and stop giving them your time and energy. When you let them go, you’ll find yourself spending more time in more places that are healthier for you. By eliminating the things that are keeping you from your identity, you will only have important things left in front of you. Knowing who we are is hard. It’s really hard. So, eliminate who you are not, first. Then, you’re going to find where you need to be and who you truly are.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?
choices: The director's offer of additional scenes was turned down.
Problems in some scenes were noticed as soon as the film was released.
Recognizing the places we don't fit in is regarded as less valuable than recognizing where we belong.
Letting go of friends who have a bad influence on us will lead us to healthier environments.
We are advised to find our real selves before removing what does not suit us.

오답
① 추가 장면에 대한 감독의 제안은 거절되었다. (→‘I’는 신이 나서 그 제안을 수락했다.)
② 영화가 개봉되자마자 일부 장면의 문제점이 발견되었다. (→몇 년 전에 그 영화를 다시 보았을 때 자신의 캐릭터가 어울리지 않는 두 개의 장면이 있다는 것을 깨달았다.)

⑤ 우리는 우리에게 맞지 않는 것을 제거하기 전에 우리의 진정한 자아를 찾으라는 조언을 받는다. (→먼저 자신이 아닌 존재를 제거할 때, 자신이 있어야 할 곳과 진정한 자신을 찾게 될 것이라는 조언을 받는다.)

body:
Number three. Give your fears credit. You know what? I try to scare myself at least once a day. I get butterflies in my stomach every morning before I go to work. I was nervous before I got here to speak tonight. I think fear is an asset because it increases our need to dare ourselves to overcome that fear. Suppose you have a fear of rejection. You want to ask somebody out, but you fear that he or she may react cynically. Well, instead of denying your fears, don’t be embarrassed to admit them and give them the credit they deserve. Don’t act like they’re no big deal and don’t deny that they exist, abandoning your opportunity to overcome them. I believe that we’re all destined to have to do the thing we fear the most anyway, at some point in our lives. So, confront your fears and give them credit, and you will find the courage to overcome them. Be brave. Have courage and get over your fears. When you do that, you get stronger, you get more aware, and you get more respect for yourself.
I hope you find joy in the process of doing what you’re meant to do. Find your identity by eliminating who you are not. Move forward, overcoming your fears. You are the author of the book on your life. So even if you make mistakes, turn the page and just keep living. Thank you and good luck.
다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Fear is something valuable that pushes us to challenge ourselves.
Denying our fears helps protect the chance to get over them.
Everyone is bound to face their greatest fear sooner or later.
Overcoming our fears allows us to become stronger and to value ourselves more.
Making mistakes is no reason to stop moving forward with our lives.

ⓐ ‘~인 것 같다, ~인 것으로 보이다’라는 뜻의 ‘seem+to부정사’에서 주절과 같은 시점의 동작이나 상태를 나타낼 경우 단순부정사(to+동사원형)를 사용하고 주절보다 이전일 경우는 완료부정사(to+have+p.p.)를 사용하며, ‘채취되었던 것’이 seems가 나타내는 현재보다 이전 과거의 일이므로, to 뒤에 수동형 완료부정사(to+have+been+p.p.)를 이루는 have been이 알맞다.
ⓑ ‘so+형용사구’인 so precious and scarce 뒤에서 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절(only ~ afford it)을 이끌고 있으므로, ‘매우 ~해서 …하다’라는 뜻의 ‘so+형용사(구)/부사(구)+that+완전한 절’ 구문을 이루는 접속사 that이 알맞다.

body:
As more countries begin to eat gim, it is being consumed in new ways depending on the country. For example, in the United States, as Americans are paying more attention to gim as a healthy food, they enjoy roasted gim snacks with almonds and coconut added. Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid. What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim. It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. So (A)[desired / devalued] was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was (B)[medical / environmental]. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it (C)[elaborated / restricted] one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?

choices: desired / medical / elaborated
desired / medical / restricted

devalued / environmental / restricted

solution:

devalued 평가절하된
(B) 흑후추는 사람들이 잘 자고, 음식을 소화하고 일광 화상과 통증으로부터의 피부 자극을 완화하는 데 도움이 되는 치료제라고 여겨졌다는 구체적 설명이 뒤에 이어지므로, 흑후추가 과거 높이 평가된 두 번째 이유는 의학적인 것이라는 흐름이 되는 medical(의학적인)이 알맞다.
environmental 환경적인
(C) 책상 위에 흑후추를 두는 것은 부와 품위의 상징이었다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 흑후추가 사회적 지위와 부를 명시적으로 나타냈다는 흐름이 되는 elaborated(~을 상세히 말했다)가 알맞다.

body:
The future of the gim industry appears bright, as global demand for gim is expected to rise in the coming years for a couple of reasons. First of all, gim is a highly valued product on the global market as a healthy food due to its nutritional properties. One hundred grams of gim contain sixteen times more dietary fiber than the same amount of cabbage, two times more protein than beans, and four times more calcium than milk. Gim’s high nutrient content will make it a popular choice among consumers who are keenly interested in a healthy diet. Second, gim is environmentally friendly. A French magazine once published an article titled “Koreans who cook seaweed for Earth,” which listed seaweed, including gim, as one of the most valuable foods for future generations, along with Spanish tomatoes, Latin American beans, and Canadian salmon. In fact, research shows that seaweed has been shown to capture and store CO₂ as it grows. For example, one ton of seaweed absorbs three times as much CO₂ as a maple tree. As demonstrated here, gim has many benefits. Who knows? There may come a day when gim is found on every dinner table around the world.

This is a NASA satellite image of the area near Wando, taken from space. NASA initially wondered what the black lines were and later discovered they are farms that grow gim. From this picture, you can guess that Korea is currently producing a lot of gim. It is relatively cheap and is frequently used in various Korean dishes, such as gimbap (a type of seaweed rice roll), gimjaban (roasted seaweed), and gimbugak (a type of crispy seaweed and rice chip). (A)그러나, 그것은 과거에는 매우 비쌌고, 오늘날 사람들이 즐길 수 있는 만큼 모든 사람들이 즐길 수는 없었습니다.
Gim in the Past
Gim seems to have been harvested in the past by women who walked into the sea during low tide to collect it from rocks. It was so precious and scarce that only royalty, like kings and queens, and the very wealthy had the privilege to afford it. During the Joseon period, ten sheets of gim were said to cost twenty cotton rolls, which cost a lot at the time. So you can imagine how expensive gim was. You might be wondering how gim became more affordable and readily available in recent years. Two figures are behind the striking popularity of gim today.

Due to its extreme rarity, gim was once difficult to obtain even for the wealthy, except for royalty.
During the Joseon Dynasty, ten sheets of gim were worth the equivalent of twenty cotton rolls.

Did you know that gim is also eaten in South Africa? In the first half of 2017, Korean gim accounted for approximately 43% of the South African market. Not surprisingly, Korea is the world’s largest gim producer and exporter, dominating roughly 70% of the global gim market. According to Graph 1, gim exports overseas were only $100 million in 2010, but have steadily increased year after year, and reached $600 million in 2020. To where is gim exported? In 2019, the top three export destinations for Korean gim were the United States, Japan, and China. Furthermore, the number of export destinations is continuously increasing. According to Graph 2, gim was only exported to 64 countries in 2010, but by September 2021, gim exports had expanded to 112 countries worldwide.

Foreign sales of gim surged from $100 million in 2010 to $600 million a decade later through continuous annual growth.
As of 2019, the United States, Japan, and China were the three smallest importers of Korean gim.
The global reach of Korean gim expanded from 64 nations in 2010 to 112 countries by September 2021.

solution:

body:
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed attached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found it ⓐ[to be / being] delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea where he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, but (A)그것은 오늘날 우리가 소비하는 만큼의 많은 김을 재배하기에 충분히 생산적이지 않았습니다.

ⓑ[For / To] our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to ⓒ[cultivate / cultivating] frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

윗글의 괄호 ⓐ, ⓑ, ⓒ에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
ⓐ / ⓑ / ⓒ
choices: to be / For / cultivating
to be / To / cultivate
being / For / cultivating
to be / To / cultivating
being / For / cultivate
solution:
ⓐ ‘~가 …인 것을 알게 되다[알아차리다]’라는 뜻으로 ‘find+목적어+(to be+)보어’를 사용하므로, 과거형으로 쓰인 found와 목적어인 대명사 it 뒤에 to부정사인 to be가 알맞다.
ⓑ 뒤에 이어진 소유격 our와 추상명사 surprise와 함께 ‘우리에게 놀랍게도’라는 뜻의 표현을 이루어야 하며, ‘~에게 …하게도’라는 뜻은 ‘to+소유격+추상명사’로 나타내므로, 전치사 To가 알맞다.
ⓒ 흐름상 전치사 to 뒤에 명사(구)가 목적어로 이어져 ‘~을 …에 붙이다’를 뜻하는 ‘attach ~ to …’ 표현을 이루어야 하므로, ‘경작’을 뜻하는 동사파생명사로 뒤의 명사 frames와 함께 ‘경작용 틀들’을 뜻하는 명사구를 이루는 cultivating이 알맞다.

As more countries begin to eat gim, it is being consumed in new ways depending on the country. For example, in the United States, as Americans are paying more attention to gim as a healthy food, they enjoy roasted gim snacks with almonds and coconut added. Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid. What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim. It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

Thailand imports Korean gim and relies entirely on traditional Korean recipes to produce its gim products.
A world-renowned culinary school released a cookbook featuring various recipes that incorporate gim into different foods.
Gim serves not only as an ingredient for novel dishes but also as a flavor enhancer for conventional meals.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was ______. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. So desired was pepper that it earned fancy nicknames like “black gold” and “king of spices.” There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it elaborated one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

a commonly found plant cultivated exclusively for medical use
a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford
a cheap flavoring agent that lost its popularity due to its strong scent
an overrated agricultural product that caused severe economic crises

solution:
ⓑ what → that[which] 또는 what 삭제 (타동사 afford뒤에 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절 ‘peasants could not afford’를 이끌어, 선행사인 명사구 a rare and expensive luxury item을 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 선행사를 포함한 관계대명사 what을 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 고치거나, 목적격 관계대명사는 생략 가능하므로 what을 삭제한다.)
*원래 지문에는 that이 쓰였음
ⓒ pepper was → was pepper (보어인 형용사구 So desired가 강조되어 문두에 쓰였으므로 ‘동사’ 도치를 적용한 ‘so+형용사+be동사+주어~’의 어순이 되도록 pepper was를 was pepper로 고친다.)
ⓕ Consider → Considering (완전한 절(it ~ commodity) 앞에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 동사원형으로 시작하는 명령문 형태의 절이 올 수 없으므로, ‘~을 고려하면’이라는 뜻으로 전치사 역할을 하며 비인칭독립분사구를 이끌도록 동사원형 Consider를 Considering으로 고친다.)
오답
ⓓ 동사원형 sleep, digest와 ‘A, B, and C‘의 병렬구조로 연결되어 ‘help+목적어+목적격보어(동사원형/to부정사)(~가 …하도록 돕다)’의 5형식 구문을 이루고 있으므로, 동사원형 relieve는 알맞다.
ⓖ ‘훨씬’이라는 의미로 쓰여 비교급 more를 강조하는 a lot은 알맞다. 참고로, 비교급을 강조하는 부사(구)로 a lot, much, far, even, still 등이 쓰인다.

G: (A)Are you aware that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
B: No, what is it?
G: It’s the kangaroo rat, and it lives in the desert in North America.
B: Really? How does it manage to survive without water?
G: Apparently, it obtains all the moisture it needs from the seeds it eats.
B: That’s fascinating! Do you know why it is called the kangaroo rat?
G: Yes, that’s because it has really long legs that help it jump really high like a kangaroo.
B: Oh, that’s cool! How high can it jump?
G: It can jump up to about 2.75 m in a single leap!
B: Wow, that’s amazing!
다음 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)와 흐름상 바꿔 쓸 수 없는 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: Are you sure there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Is it true that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Have you heard that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Do you know that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
Did you realize that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
solution:
밑줄 친 (A) ‘물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것을 알고 있니?’는 ‘Are you aware that ~?(~라는 것을 알고 있니?)’을 사용해 상대방이 어떤 정보나 사실에 대해 알고 있는지 묻고 있는 것이므로, 확실성 여부를 묻는 ‘Are you sure (that) ~?(~라는 것이 확실하니?)’을 사용한 ① ‘물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것이 확실하니?’와 진위 여부를 묻는 ‘Is it true (that) ~(~라는 것이 사실이니?)’을 사용한 ② ’물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것이 사실이니?‘와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.
오답

④ 물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 것을 알고 있니?
⑤ 물을 마시지 않고도 생존할 수 있는 동물이 있다는 사실에 대해 알고 있었니?

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.” However, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park ______. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making it nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: are fairly high
are slim to none
are difficult to predict
are worth taking seriously
are greater than those of other redwoods
solution:
공원은 방문객들로 인한 잠재적 피해로부터 나무를 보호하기 위해 나무의 정확한 위치를 비밀로 유지한다고 했으며, Hyperion과 인접한 redwood 간의 높이 차이가 단지 몇 미터에 불과해 지상에서 식별하는 것이 거의 불가능하다고 설명하므로, 공원에서 실제로 Hyperion을 보게 될 가능성이 매우 낮다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘거의 희박한’이 알맞다.
오답
① 꽤 높은
③ 예측하기 어려운
④ 진지하게 생각해볼 가치가 있다
⑤ 다른 redwood를 볼 가능성보다 훨씬 크다

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants ______. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.
다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: release their seeds only after the fruits have fully developed
only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience
require the help of animals such as birds to release their seeds effectively
continuously release their seeds throughout the year regardless of the weather conditions
release their seeds gradually over an extended period of time to maximize their chances of survival
solution:
사례로 든 eucalyptus의 경우, 씨앗이 강한 껍질로 보호되어 있어 새들이 먹을 수 없으나 덥고 건조한 날씨에 잎에 불이 붙으면 강한 열로 인해 단단한 껍질이 갈라지고, 그때 씨앗이 껍질에서 나와 땅에 떨어지고 자라기 시작하며, 타고 남은 재가 그것들을 가혹한 환경에서 보호하는 한편 다른 경쟁 식물들을 태운다고 설명했으므로, 성숙한 씨앗이 자동으로 모체 식물에서 분리되는 대부분의 식물과 달리 eucalyptus와 같은 일부 식물은 극한의 환경 조건을 거쳐야만 씨앗을 방출한다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘극심한 경험을 견딘 후에야 씨앗을 방출합니다’가 알맞다.
오답

body:
Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and ⓐbury it in the ground to eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are ⓑquite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓒwere antelope dung. That is why dung beetles ⓓoften spot rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the ⓔconfusing beetles will realize ⓕthey cannot. They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓕ 중, 어법상 어색한 것의 개수는?
choices: 1개
2개
3개
4개
5개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 2개이다.
ⓓ often spot → are often spotted (why가 이끄는 절의 주어 dung beetles가 ‘발견되는’ 대상이며, 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’spot+목적어+목적격보어(현재분사)(~가 …하는 것을 발견하다)‘의 목적격보어에 해당하는 현재분사구(rolling ~ balls)가 이어져 있으므로, 수동태 ’be spotted+현재분사(…하는 것이 발견되다)‘를 이루도록 often spotted를 are often spotted로 고친다.)
ⓔ confusing → confused (정관사 the와 명사 beetles 사이에 뒤의 명사를 수식하는 형용사가 쓰인 것은 알맞으나, 수식받는 명사가 ’혼란스럽게 하는‘ 주체가 아니라 ’혼란스럽게 된‘ 대상이므로, 능동의 의미를 가진 현재분사 형태의 형용사 confusing을 수동의 의미를 가진 과거분사 형태의 형용사 confused로 고친다.)
오답
ⓒ as if가 이끄는 조건절이 현재 사실의 반대를 가정해야 하므로, ‘as if+주어+were/동사의 과거형 ~(마치 ~인 것처럼)’ 형태의 가정법 과거 표현을 이루는 동사 were는 알맞다.
ⓕ 동사 realize의 목적어이므로 명사절 접속사 that이 생략된 완전한 절의 형태가 되어야 하나, 조동사 뒤에 반복을 피하기 위해 동사구의 나머지 부분을 생략할 수 있으므로, ’they cannot eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them’에서 반복되는 ‘eat ~ them’을 생략한 형태인 they cannot은 알맞다.

solution:

body:
Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks.
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. (A) Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. (B) Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. (C) Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. (D) Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. (E) As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.
다음 글의 (A)~(E) 중, 주어진 문장이 들어갈 알맞은 곳은?
solution: 주어진 문장은 ‘분홍색 트럼펫을 닮은 이 식물의 꽃은 결국 많은 갈고리가 있는 열매로 변합니다.’라는 뜻으로, Its가 가리키는 devil’s claw를 날카로운 갈고리나 바늘을 갖춘 식물의 예시로 소개하며 그것의 서식지를 설명한 다음이자, 주어진 문장에 언급된 fruits를 these fruits로 가리켜, 꽃이 열매로 변한 이후의 과정에 해당하는 내용으로서 이 열매들이 마르는 동안 단단해지고 갈고리들이 동물의 몸에 달라붙을 만큼 단단해진다고 설명하는 문장 앞인 (E)에 들어가는 것이 알맞다.

body:
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for (A)[distributing / storing] their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts (B)[untouched / decomposed]. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a (C)[satisfying / dissatisfying] meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.
다음 글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: distributing untouched satisfying
distributing untouched dissatisfying
distributing decomposed satisfying
storing untouched dissatisfying
storing decomposed satisfying
solution:
(A) 달콤한 향기로 동물들을 유혹해 과육과 함께 씨앗을 먹게 하고, 씨앗들이 배변을 통해 내보내져 발아하고 자라며 퍼진다고 설명하므로, 식물들이 씨앗을 퍼뜨리는 대가로 동물들에게 맛있는 먹이를 제공한다는 흐름이 되는 distributing(~을 퍼뜨리는)이 알맞다.
storing ~을 보관[저장]하는
(B) 씨앗들이 배변을 통해 내보내져 발아하고 자라기 시작한다는 내용이 뒤에 이어지므로, 씨앗이 소화되지 않고 훼손되지 않은 원래의 상태 그대로 동물들의 소화관을 통과한다는 흐름이 되는 untouched(훼손되지 않은, 원래 그대로의)가 알맞다.
decomposed 분해된
(C) jackfruit의 달콤한 향기에 이끌려 동물들이 그것의 맛있는 과육을 먹고, 함께 섭취한 씨앗이 배변으로 내보내져 발아하고 자란다고 설명하므로, 만족스러운 식사의 대가로 동물들이 씨앗을 퍼뜨린다는 흐름이 되는 satisfying(만족스러운)이 알맞다.
dissatisfying 만족을 주지 못하는

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell (A)[cracking / to crack] open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. ⓐ떨어진 씨앗들은 편리하게도 화재 후 남은 부드러운 재 속에 감춰지는데, 이것은 그것들을 가혹한 환경으로부터 보호합니다. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also (B)[burns / burning] practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided (C)[that / what] there is fire.
윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: cracking burning that
to crack burning what
to crack burns that
cracking burns that
to crack burns what
solution:
(A) 동사 causes와 목적어 the shell에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, ‘cause+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 유발하다)’의 5형식 구문에 쓰일 때 cause는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하는 동사이므로, to부정사인 to crack이 알맞다.
(B) 주어 Wildfire와 두 개의 콤마(,) 사이에 삽입되어 주어를 부연 설명하는 과거분사구(often started ~ tree)에 이어져 있으며, 뒤에 다른 동사구 없이 destroying 이하의 분사구문이 이어지므로, 주어에 대한 동사가 올 자리이다. 따라서 단수인 주어에 수일치한 단수동사 burns가 알맞다.
(C) ‘만약 ~한다면, ~라는 것을 조건으로’라는 뜻의 ‘provided (that)+완전한 절’ 형태의 부사절을 이루어야 하므로 that이 알맞다.

body:
Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it (A)spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to (B)elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much (C)farther from the parent tree. The rotation also (D)slow down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps (E)cause the damage to the seed during the fall.
다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 어색한 것은?
solution: (E) cause(~을 유발하다) → reduce(~을 줄이다)

body:
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly ⓐattached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The ⓑattached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them ⓒto feel like the devil is scratching ⓓthem with its horrifying claws. That is ⓔhow devil’s claw became known as the worst free rider.
윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓒ to feel → feel (현재분사 형태로 쓰인 making과 목적어 them에 이어진 목적격보어 자리이며, make가 사역동사로 쓰여 ‘~가 …하게 만들다’를 뜻하는 ‘make+목적어+목적격보어’의 5형식 구문을 이룰 때, 목적어와 목적격보어의 관계가 능동인 경우 목적격보어로 동사원형이 쓰이고, 목적어 them이 가리키는 the animals가 ‘느끼는’ 주체이므로, to feel을 능동 관계를 나타내는 동사원형 feel로 고친다.)
오답
ⓐ ‘~가 계속 …하게 하다’라는 뜻의 5형식 구문인 ‘keep+목적어+목적격보어‘에서 목적격보어 자리에 분사(구)가 올 수 있으며, 목적어인 the dried fruit이 attach(~을 붙이다)의 대상이고 뒤에 목적어 없이 ’attach ~ to …(~을 …에 붙이다)‘의 전치사 to가 바로 이어졌으므로, 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 attached는 알맞다. 참고로, 부사 firmly가 앞에서 수식하고 있다.

body:
G: Andrew, (A)you’ve got to watch this video!
B: Wow, a female seahorse is giving birth to a cluster of babies!
G: Actually, it’s the male seahorse, not the female.
B: Wait, (B)do you mean the male seahorse gets pregnant?
G: (C)To be precise, the female seahorse lays her eggs into an inflatable pouch on the front of the male’s tail, and he fertilizes and carries them.
B: (D)That’s incredible! Do you know how long the male seahorse carries the eggs?
G: (E)I’ve heard it’s about two to four weeks until they hatch and are ready to be released.
B: That’s really interesting.
G: Nature is truly full of wonders.

다음 대화의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E)와 흐름상 바꾸어 쓸 수 없는 것은?
choices: (A): you should check out this video
(B): did you say
(C): To put it simply
(D): That’s unbelievable!
(E): I’ve been told that
solution:
(C) To be precise는 ‘자세하게 말하면’이라는 뜻으로, 수컷 해마가 임신을 한다는 말에 대해 암컷 해마가 수컷 꼬리의 새끼 주머니에 알을 낳고 수컷이 알을 수정시켜 지니고 다닌다고 구체적으로 정확히 설명하기 위해 쓰였으므로, ‘간단히 말하면, 쉽게 말하면’이라는 뜻으로 앞서 한 설명을 요약하거나 더 쉽게 정리해 말할 때 사용하는 To put it simply와는 바꾸어 쓸 수 없다.
오답
(A) 너는 이 영상을 꼭 봐야 해 = 너는 이 영상을 봐야 해
(B) 네 말은 ~라는 뜻이야? = 방금 ~라고 했어?

(E) ~라고 들었어 = ~라고 들었어

body:
Plants are amazing. Throughout their long existence, they have created diverse survival strategies. Seeds, in particular, are one of the strongest survival techniques (A)[which / by which] they have developed. Let’s discover the fascinating and mysterious world of seeds.
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby (B)[gets / getting] them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin (C)[sprouting / to sprout] and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
choices: which / gets / sprouting
which / getting / sprouting
by which / gets / sprouting
which / getting / to sprout
by which / getting / to sprout
solution:
(A) 목적어가 없는 불완전한 절(they have developed)을 이끌어 선행사인 명사구 the strongest survival techniques를 수식하는 관계사절을 이루어야 하므로, 목적격 관계대명사 which가 알맞다. 참고로, ‘전치사+관계대명사’ 뒤에는 완전한 절이 온다.
본문변형 (A)는 목적격 관계대명사 which 또는 that으로 원래 지문에서 생략되어 있음
(B) 동사가 있는 완전한 절(It tempts ~ flesh)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 다른 동사(구)가 연결될 수 없으므로, thereby 이하는 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 분사구문의 형태가 되어야 한다. 뒤에 목적어인 them과 목적격보어인 to부정사구(to eat the seeds)가 이어져 ’get+목적어+목적격보어(to부정사)(~가 …하게 하다)‘의 능동태 5형식 구문을 이루고 있으므로, 현재분사 getting이 알맞다.
(C) begin의 목적어로 동명사나 to부정사가 둘 다 쓰일 수 있으나, 뒤에 등위접속사 and로 to가 생략된 동사원형 grow가 병렬로 연결되어 있으므로, to부정사인 to sprout가 알맞다.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 (A)~(E) 중, 흐름상 관계없는 문장은?
solution: 날카로운 갈고리나 바늘을 사용해 지나가는 동물에게 씨앗을 붙여 그것을 퍼뜨리는 식물의 사례로 devil’s claw를 소개하며 분홍색 트럼펫을 닮은 그것의 꽃이 많은 갈고리가 있는 열매로 변한다고 설명을 시작한 뒤에, 열매가 마르는 동안 갈고리들이 동물들의 털에 달라붙을 만큼 단단해지고, 동물들이 이동하면서 여러 장소에 씨앗이 흩어지게 되며, 그 과정에서 동물들은 갈고리로 인해 심한 통증을 느낀다는 내용으로 이어지는 것이 자연스러우므로, devil’s claw의 씨앗이 퍼지는 방식과 무관하게 씨앗이 발아하기 위한 환경 조건을 언급하는 (D) ‘떨어진 씨앗은 충분한 수분과 햇빛에 노출될 때 발아할 수 있다.’는 전체 글의 흐름과 관계없다.

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy to find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, which was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. (A)______, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height that they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.” (B)______, the odds of you seeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, (C)______. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.

윗글의 빈칸 (A), (B)에 들어갈 알맞은 말로 연결된 것은?
choices: In short / Actually
However / Consequently
Moreover / For example
However / In fact
Furthermore / As a result
solution:
(A) Hyperion이 발견되기 전에는 Helios가 가장 높은 나무로 여겨졌다는 내용 뒤에, 2006년에 두 명의 자연학자가 Helios보다 더 높은 나무를 발견했다는 내용이 이어져 흐름이 반전되므로, 역접을 나타내는 However(하지만)가 알맞다.
(B) Helios보다 더 높은 나무가 발견되어 그리스 신화의 Titan 중 ‘가장 높은 자’를 의미하는 Hyperion의 이름을 따서 그 나무의 이름이 지어졌다는 내용 뒤에, 공원에서 Hyperion을 볼 가능성은 희박하다는 예상과 다른 대조적인 사실을 연결하므로, In fact(사실은)가 알맞다.
본문변형 (B)는 원래 지문에서 However였음
오답
① 요컨대 실제로는, 사실은
② 하지만 그 결과, 따라서
③ 게다가, 더욱이 예를 들어
⑤ 게다가, 더욱이 그 결과로

body:
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Many plants provide animals with food in return for spreading their seeds.
Some plants spread their seeds by attaching them to passing animals, using hooks or needles.
Devil's claw is considered the most ruthless among plants that use hooks to spread seeds.
The flowers of Devil's claw, which look like pink trumpets, become fruits with many hooks.
Once the fruits of devil’s claw dry out, their hooks become weaker and fall off the animals’ fur.
solution:
devil’s claw의 열매는 마르는 동안에 단단해지고, 갈고리들은 동물의 몸에 달라붙을 만큼 단단해진다고 했으므로, ⑤ ‘devil’s claw의 열매가 말라버리고 나면 그것의 갈고리들은 힘이 약해져 동물들의 털에서 떨어진다.‘는 일치하지 않는 내용이다.
오답
① 많은 식물들은 자신들의 씨앗을 퍼뜨려 주는 대가로 동물들에게 먹이를 제공한다.
② 몇몇 식물들은 갈고리나 가시를 이용해 지나가는 동물들에게 자신들의 씨앗을 붙임으로써 씨앗을 퍼뜨린다.
③ Devil’s claw는 씨앗을 퍼뜨리기 위해 갈고리를 사용하는 식물들 중 가장 무자비한 식물로 여겨진다.
④ 분홍색 트럼펫처럼 생긴 Devil’s claw의 꽃은 많은 갈고리가 달린 열매가 된다.

body:
Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or ⓐlay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size.
(A) That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and ⓑsmell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of ⓒthem, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot.
(B) They cannot help aborting and ⓓsearch for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.
(C) Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓔhad been antelope dung.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 고르면?
solution:
ⓓ search →searching (aborting과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되어 ‘~할 수밖에 없다’라는 뜻의 ‘cannot help -ing‘ 구문을 이루어야 하므로, search를 -ing 형태의 searching으로 고친다.)
본문변형 have no choice but to abort and search → cannot help aborting and searching
ⓔ had been → were (현재시제로 쓰인 앞의 완전한 절(they carefully roll the seed away)에 이어진 as if가 이끄는 절의 동사 자리이며, 흐름상 앞 절과 동일한 현재 시점에서 반대의 사실을 가정해야 하므로, ‘as if+주어+were/과거동사 ~(마치 ~인 것처럼)’ 형태의 가정법 과거 표현을 이루어야 한다. 따라서 had been을 were로 고친다. 참고로, ‘as if+주어+had been ~’은 ‘마치 ~였던 것처럼’이라는 뜻으로 과거 사실의 반대를 가정할 때 쓰인다.
오답
ⓐ 목적을 나타내는 부사적 용법의 to부정사구인 to eat 이하에서 동사원형 eat와 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되므로 동사원형이 올 자리이며, 뒤에 목적어인 명사 eggs가 이어져 있으므로, 능동태 동사원형 lay는 알맞다.

body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically ⓐseparated from the parent plant. However, some plants only release their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they ⓑare bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally ⓒcatching fire because the leaves contain highly flammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, ⓓhitting the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently concealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often ⓔstarted by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight ⓕneeding for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce ⓖprovided there is fire.

다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓒ catching → catch (주어 eucalyptus leaves에 수일치한 복수동사 rub과 등위접속사 and에 의해 병렬로 연결되며 부사 naturally의 수식을 받는 동사가 올 자리이므로, catching을 복수동사 catch로 고친다.)
ⓓ hitting → hit (주어 the seeds에 수일치한 복수동사 come, begin과 ‘A, B, and C’의 형태로 병렬로 연결되어야 하므로, hitting을 복수동사 hit으로 고친다.)
ⓕ needing → needed (for의 목적어로 쓰인 명사구 the water and sunlight을 수식하는 분사구를 이루는 분사가 올 자리이며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘필요로 하는’ 주체가 아니라 ‘필요시되는’ 대상이며 뒤에 이어진 목적어가 없으므로, 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 needing을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 needed로 고친다.)
오답
ⓑ 주어 they가 가리키는 Eucalyptus seeds가 ‘타동사+부사’ 구조의 구동사 ‘bind ~ together(~을 묶다)‘의 대상이며, 목적어 없이 부사 together만 뒤에 쓰였으므로, 수동태인 ’be bound together‘를 사용한 are bound는 알맞다.
ⓖ ‘만약 ~한다면, ~라는 것을 조건으로’라는 뜻으로 뒤의 완전한 절(there is fire)을 이끌어 ‘provided (that)+완전한 절’ 형태의 조건 부사절을 이루고 있으며, provided that에서 that은 생략 가능하므로, provided는 알맞다.
본문변형 provided that → provided

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓖ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 모두 골라 짝지은 것은?
solution:
ⓑ attaching → attached (전치사 with 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 some seaweed가 온 뒤, 부대상황을 나타내는 ‘with+명사(구)+분사(구)(~가 …한 상태로)’를 이루는 분사구 또는 ‘~가 있는’이라는 뜻으로 쓰인 전치사 with의 목적어인 명사구 some seaweed를 수식하는 분사구가 이어지는 것은 알맞으나, 앞의 명사구가 ‘부착된’ 대상이므로, ‘attach ~ to …(~을 …에 부착하다)’의 수동 표현인 ‘~ be attached to …(~가 …에 부착되다)’를 사용해 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 attaching을 수동을 나타내는 과거분사 attached로 고친다.)
ⓓ enough productive → productive enough (enough가 부사로 쓰여 형용사나 부사를 수식할 때, 형용사/부사의 뒤에 위치하므로, enough productive를 productive enough의 어순으로 고친다. 그 외, was의 보어로 형용사 productive가 쓰인 것과, ‘형용사/부사+enough+to부정사(구)(~할 만큼 충분히 …한/…하게)’를 이루는 to부정사 to cultivate는 모두 알맞다.)
ⓔ us → our (‘~에게 …하게도’라는 뜻은 ‘to+소유격+추상명사’로 나타내므로, 전치사 To와 추상명사 surprise 사이에 쓰인 목적격 형태의 us를 소유격인 our로 고친다.)
오답
ⓕ 주절(she discovered ~) 앞에 콤마(,)와 함께 분사구문이 쓰일 수 있으며, 의미를 명확히 하기 위해 접속사를 남겨둔 ‘접속사+분사~’ 형태로 쓸 수 있고, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 she가 타동사로 쓰인 research(~을 연구하다)의 주체이고, 뒤에 목적어로 명사구 the annual life cycle of seaweed가 있으므로, 접속사 While 뒤에 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 researching이 쓰인 While researching은 알맞다.

Did you know that gim is also eaten in South Africa? In the first half of 2017, Korean gim accounted for approximately 43% of the South African market. Not surprisingly, Korea is the world’s largest gim producer and exporter, dominating roughly 70% of the global gim market. According to Graph 1, gim exports overseas were only $100 million in 2010, but have steadily increased year after year, and reached $600 million in 2020. To where is gim exported? In 2019, the top three export destinations for Korean gim were the United States, Japan, and China. Furthermore, the number of export destinations is continuously increasing. According to Graph 2, gim was only exported to 64 countries in 2010, but by September 2021, gim exports had expanded to 112 countries worldwide.
As more countries begin to eat gim, it is being consumed in new ways depending on the country. For example, in the United States, as Americans are paying more attention to gim as a healthy food, they enjoy roasted gim snacks with almonds and coconut added. Also, Thailand is producing its own gim snacks by importing gim from Korea and processing it with popular Thai flavors, such as tom yam kung (a sweet and sour flavor) and grilled squid. What is more, gim can be easily added to a variety of dishes. For example, the Culinary Institute of America, an internationally famous culinary university, published a recipe book titled Fabulous and Flavorful Gim. It includes gim recipes, such as gim flavored popcorn, gim fried chicken, and even gim ice cream. It is quite clear that gim is being used to create new and delicious types of food and to give new flavors to old favorites.

body:
It is widely believed that during the reign of King Injo, a man named Yeoik Gim succeeded in farming gim for the first time in history. He was taking a walk along the beach near the Seomjin River one day. He came across floating tree branches with some seaweed attached to them. He tasted the seaweed out of curiosity and found it to be delicious. The following year, he planted some poles along the sea where he had discovered the seaweed. Floating seaweed became entangled in the poles and grew there. This method allowed more people to enjoy gim, ______.
To our surprise, a British scientist named Kathleen Drew-Baker, who had never been to Korea, contributed to making gim more widely available. While researching the annual life cycle of seaweed, she discovered how seaweed reproduces through spores, which function like seeds. Since her research, people have been able to produce gim in large quantities by artificially collecting spores and attaching them to cultivating frames. That is how gim became more affordable and widely available these days.

윗글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: so it completely replaced natural collection methods in a very short period
but it was not productive enough to cultivate as much gim as we consume today
but it led to severe conflicts among local fishermen over farming territories
which resulted in a sharp decrease in the quality and flavor of cultivated gim
and it immediately made gim one of the most exported items to neighboring countries
solution:
다음 단락에 영국 과학자 Kathleen Drew-Baker의 포자를 통한 번식 방법 덕에 김의 대량 생산이 가능해져서 김이 더욱 저렴해지고 널리 보급되었다는 내용이 이어지므로, 김여익의 양식법 덕분에 더 많은 사람이 김을 즐길 수 있게 되었지만, 그 방법을 통해 김을 대량 생산하는 것에는 한계가 있었다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘하지만 그것은 오늘날 우리가 소비하는 만큼의 많은 김을 재배하기에 충분히 생산적이지 않았다’가 알맞다.

body:
Black pepper is recognized for its contribution to countless styles of world cuisine in general and is one of the most commonly used spices in the world. However, in the past, it was a rare and expensive luxury item that peasants could not afford. In some parts of the world, people paid rents and taxes with black pepper. (A)후추는 너무 열망되어 그것은 ‘블랙 골드’와 ‘향신료의 제왕’ 같은 화려한 별명을 얻었습니다. There are several reasons black pepper was highly regarded in the past. First, before toothbrushes and toothpaste were invented, people used spices to reduce bad breath. Another reason was medical. It was believed that pepper was a healing remedy that helped people sleep well, digest food, and relieve skin irritation from sunburn and aches. The third reason is that it elaborated one’s social status and wealth. Having pepper on one’s desk was a symbol of wealth and dignity. Thus, not only did black pepper make food more delicious, but it also meant better-smelling breath, better health, and greater wealth and elite position in society. Considering all these, it is clear why black pepper was such a highly valued commodity. While some might feel that black pepper is just like any other spice, it is pretty obvious that black pepper, (B)both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye.

윗글의 밑줄 친 (B)both in and outside the kitchen, has a lot more to offer than meets the eye가 의미하는 바로 알맞은 것은?
choices: has lost its high economic value as alternative spices enter the market
is valued primarily for its ability to preserve food and extend its shelf life
has gained popularity across the world not only for its flavor but also for its affordability
is now used by anyone to treat serious health problems, regardless of social status or income
serves not only as a culinary ingredient but also as a versatile item with value in terms of health and social status

body:
Gim in the Future
The future of the gim industry appears bright, as global demand for gim is expected to rise in the coming years for a couple of reasons. First of all, gim is a highly valued product on the global market as a healthy food due to its nutritional properties. One hundred grams of gim contain sixteen times more dietary fiber than the same amount of cabbage, two times more protein than beans, and four times more calcium than milk. Gim’s high nutrient content will make it a popular choice among consumers who are keenly interested in a healthy diet. Second, gim is environmentally friendly. A French magazine once published an article titled “Koreans who cook seaweed for Earth,” which listed seaweed, including gim, as one of the most valuable foods for future generations, along with Spanish tomatoes, Latin American beans, and Canadian salmon. In fact, research shows that seaweed has been shown to capture and store CO₂ as it grows. For example, one ton of seaweed absorbs three times as much CO₂ as a maple tree. As demonstrated here, gim has many benefits. Who knows? There may come a day when gim is found on every dinner table around the world.

choices: What are the prospects of the gim industry in the coming years?

choices: 2개
3개
4개

6개
solution:
어법상 어색한 것은 총 3개이다.
ⓐ to be harvested → to have been harvested
(‘~인 것 같다, ~인 것으로 보이다’라는 뜻으로 ‘seem+to부정사’를 쓰며, 주어 Gim이 ‘채취되었던’ 대상이므로 seems 뒤에 수동형 to부정사가 쓰이는 것은 알맞으나, seems가 나타내는 현재보다 이전 과거의 일이므로, 수동형 완료부정사(to+have+been+p.p.)를 사용해 to be harvested를 to have been harvested로 고친다.)
ⓒ costing → to cost
(‘~라고 말해진다’라는 뜻으로 ‘be said+to부정사’를 사용하므로, 수동태인 were said 뒤의 costing을 to부정사인 to cost로 고친다.)
ⓕ enjoying → to enjoy
(’allow+목적어+목적격보어(~가 …하게 하다)‘의 5형식 구문에서 allow는 목적격보어로 to부정사를 취하므로, allowed와 목적어 more people 뒤의 목적격보어 자리에 쓰인 enjoying을 to부정사인 to enjoy로 고친다.)

G: Are you aware that there’s an animal that can survive without drinking water?
B: No, what is it?
G: It’s the kangaroo rat, and it lives in the desert in North America.
B: Really? How does it manage to survive without water?
G: Apparently, it obtains all the moisture it needs from the seeds it eats.
B: That’s fascinating! Do you know why it is called the kangaroo rat?
G: Yes, that’s because it has really long legs that help it jump really high like a kangaroo.
B: Oh, that’s cool! How high can it jump?
G: It can jump up to about 2.75 m in a single leap!
B: Wow, that’s amazing!

choices: The boy has heard about the kangaroo rat’s ability to survive without drinking water.
The kangaroo rat gets necessary moisture by drinking water stored underground.
The kangaroo rat got its name because it has a pouch similar to that of a kangaroo.
The kangaroo rat’s long legs allow the animal to jump very high.
The kangaroo rat can jump at least 2.75 m in a single leap.

It tempts animals (B)[eating / to eat] delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. body:
Out of numerous creative methods for spreading seeds, silver arrow-reed in South Africa has a particularly unique one. Silver arrow-reed spreads its seeds by deceiving dung beetles. Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground to eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it were antelope dung. That is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They have no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. By tricking dung beetles into rolling away and burying the seeds, silver arrow-reed is able to spread and plant its seeds better.

다음 글의 제목으로 알맞은 것은?
choices: How Antelope Dung Helps Plants Grow in the Wild
The Diet and Nesting Habits of Dung Beetles in South Africa
The Visual Similarities Between Seeds and Animal Waste
Why Dung Beetles Struggle to Find Real Antelope Dung
Silver Arrow-Reed‘s Tricks to Spread Seeds by Fooling Dung Beetles
solution:
남아프리카의 silver arrow-reed가 씨앗을 퍼뜨리는 독특한 방법에 관한 글로, 자신들의 씨앗이 영양 배설물과 비슷한 모양과 냄새를 가진 점을 이용해 쇠똥구리를 속여 영양 배설물 대신 씨앗을 굴리고 묻히게 함으로써 자신들의 씨앗을 퍼뜨리고 심는다는 내용을 다루고 있으므로, 글의 제목으로 ⑤ ‘쇠똥구리를 속여서 씨앗을 퍼뜨리는 Silver Arrow-Reed의 속임수’가 알맞다.
오답
① 영양 배설물은 야생에서 식물이 자라는 데 어떻게 도움이 되는가
② 남아프리카 쇠똥구리의 식습관과 둥지 습성

Many plants opt ⓐto scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants (A)______, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms ⓑresemble pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough ⓒattaching to the bodies of animals.
As animals pass by, the hooks ⓓextending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, ⓔmake them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil’s claw became ⓕknown as the worst free rider.

윗글의 빈칸 (A)에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: use insects to carry their seeds
attach their seeds to passing animals
scatter their seeds by relying on water currents

solution:
앞서 많은 식물들이 동물들에게 먹이를 제공함으로써 씨앗을 퍼뜨리지만 모든 식물들이 그런 것은 아니라고 했으며, 열매의 갈고리들이 동물의 몸에 단단히 붙어 동물들이 이동하는 동안 여러 장소로 흩어지게 되고, 이 과정에서 동물들에게 심한 통증을 유발한다는 설명이 이어지므로, 씨앗을 동물들의 몸에 붙여 이동시키는 방법을 사용해 동물들에게 아무런 보답 없이 그것들을 퍼뜨린다는 흐름이 되어야 한다. 따라서 빈칸에는 ② ‘지나가는 동물들에게 씨앗을 붙인다’가 알맞다.

③ 물살에 의존해 자신들의 씨앗을 흩뿌린다
④ 바람에 의해 이동될 수 있는 가벼운 씨앗을 만든다

Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. ______

다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 알맞은 것은?
choices: In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

solution:
세계에서 가장 큰 나무 열매인 jackfruit의 사례를 들어, 그 나무가 달콤한 향기로 동물들을 유혹하여 과육과 함께 씨앗을 먹게 하고, 씨앗이 과육과 달리 소화되지 않고 배변을 통해 밖으로 배출되어 발아하여 자라기 시작하며 jackfruit이 퍼져 나간다고 설명했으므로, 식물이 먹이를 제공한 대가로 동물들이 씨앗을 퍼뜨린다고 정리하는 흐름이 되는 ① ‘만족스러운 식사에 대한 대가로, 동물들은 jackfruit 씨앗들을 퍼뜨립니다.’가 빈칸에 알맞다.
오답
② 포식자들로부터 자신들의 씨앗을 보호하기 위해, jackfruit 나무는 불쾌한 냄새가 나는 열매를 만든다.
③ 씨앗을 jackfruit 나무에서 떨어진 곳에 퍼뜨림으로써, 동물들은 씨앗이 새로운 장소에서 자라도록 돕는다.
④ 동물들이 jackfruit 씨앗을 소화할 수 없기 때문에, 그들은 열매를 소화하기 전에 그 씨앗을 뱉는다.
⑤ 씨앗이 먹히는 것을 막기 위해, jackfruit 나무는 동물들이 열매를 열기 어렵게 만드는 단단한 겉껍질을 발달시킨다.

(A)그런 다음, 그들은 마치 그것이 영양의 배설물인 것처럼 씨앗을 조심스럽게 굴려서 갑니다. That is why dung beetles are often spotted ⓓrolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. 윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ aborting → to abort (‘~할 수밖에 없다’라는 뜻으로 ‘have no choice[option/alternative/other way] but+to부정사’, ‘cannot help -ing’, ‘cannot help but+동사원형’ 등을 사용하므로, have no choice but 뒤에 to부정사가 이어져야 한다. 따라서 동명사 aborting을 to부정사인 to abort로 고친다.)
