ⓓ 수동태 동사구 are often spotted에 이어져 있으므로, 5형식인 ’spot+목적어+목적격보어(현재분사)(~가 …하는 것을 발견하다)‘의 수동태 ’be spotted+현재분사(…하는 것이 발견되다)‘를 이루는 현재분사 rolling은 알맞다.

body:
Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms resembling pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them feel like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is how devil’s claw became known as the worst free rider.

다음 글을 아래와 같이 요약할 때, 빈칸 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?
Devil's claw, a plant inhabiting the Kalahari Desert, spreads its (A)______ by attaching its (B)______ to passing animals’ fur, and the sharp hooks on the (B)______ cause extreme (C)______ to the animals.
(A) (B) (C)
choices: seeds fruits pain
toxins leaves pain
seeds leaves pleasure
toxins fruits pain
seeds fruits pleasure
solution:
요약문 칼라하리 사막에 서식하는 식물인 devil's claw는 자신의 (B)열매를 지나가는 동물의 털에 붙여 자신의 (A)씨앗을 퍼뜨리며, (B)열매의 날카로운 갈고리들이 동물에게 극심한 (C)고통을 유발한다.
오답
② 독소 잎사귀 고통
③ 씨앗 잎사귀 쾌감
④ 독소 열매 고통
⑤ 씨앗 열매 쾌감

Eucalyptus seeds are as ⓐtiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly ⓑflammable oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to ⓒcrack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently ⓓconcealed in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, ⓔprotecting other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 알맞게 고쳐 쓰지 못한 것을 모두 고르면?
choices: ⓐ: find → to find
ⓑ: reached → reaching
ⓒ: what → which
ⓓ: see → to see
ⓔ: are → is
solution:
ⓒ what → that (‘so+형용사’인 so overwhelmed가 있는 앞 절의 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절이 뒤에 이어지므로, ‘너무 ~해서 …하다’라는 뜻의 ‘so+형용사/부사+that+완전한 절(주어+동사 ~)’ 구문을 이루도록 what을 which가 아닌 that으로 고친다.)
ⓓ see → seeing (전치사 of의 목적어인 명사(구)나 동명사(구)를 이루어야 하며, 의미상 주어 you가 목적격의 형태로 앞에 쓰였으므로, see를 to see가 아니라 동명사 seeing으로 고친다. 참고로, 전치사의 목적어 자리에 to부정사(구)는 쓸 수 없으며, to부정사의 의미상 주어는 to부정사 앞에 ‘for+목적격/명사(구)’ 형태로 쓰고, 동명사의 의미상 주어는 동명사 앞에 목적격이나 소유격의 형태로 쓴다.)
오답
ⓐ 가주어 it에 대한 진주어 자리에 to부정사(구)가 와야 하므로, 동사 find를 to부정사인 to find로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓑ 동사가 있는 완전한 절(a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall)에 접속사 없이 콤마(,)로만 동사(구)가 이어질 수 없으므로 흐름상 동시동작(~하면서)을 나타내는 분사구문을 이루는 분사 형태가 되어야 하며, 주절 주어와 동일한 분사구문의 의미상 주어 a redwood named Hyperion이 타동사 reach(~에 이르다)의 주체이고 뒤에 목적어로 over 115 m가 이어져 있으므로, reached를 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 reaching으로 고친 것은 알맞다.
ⓔ 주어 The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods 뒤에 a few meters를 보어로 하는 be동사가 올 자리이며, 주어의 핵심이 단수명사구 The height difference이므로, 수일치를 위해 복수동사 are를 단수동사 is로 고친 것은 알맞다.

body:
Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall.

⑤ 회전은 단풍나무 씨앗의 착지에 어떤 영향을 미치는가? (→낙하 속도를 늦춰 씨앗이 부드럽게 착륙하게 하며, 이는 낙하 중 씨앗에 손상을 줄이는 데 도움이 된다.)

Dung beetles, by nature, roll antelope dung and bury it in the ground ⓑto eat or lay eggs in. Silver arrow-reed seeds are dark brown, round, and slightly larger than 1 cm in size. Their visual appearance and smell are quite similar to antelope dung. So when a seed falls onto the ground, dung beetles will approach the fallen seed within minutes. Then, they carefully roll the seed away as if it ⓒwere antelope dung. ⓓThat is why dung beetles are often spotted rolling silver arrow-reed seeds that look and smell like dung balls. When they try to eat the seeds or lay eggs inside of them, however, the confused beetles will realize they cannot. They ⓔhave no choice but to abort and search for real dung balls. body:
In most cases, mature seeds are automatically separated from the parent plant. However, some plants only (A)[retain / release] their seeds after enduring an extreme experience. Eucalyptus is one such example. Eucalyptus seeds are as tiny as grains of sand, but they are bound together in firm capsules. Birds cannot eat them because they are securely protected by a strong shell. In long periods of hot and dry weather, eucalyptus leaves rub together and naturally catch fire because the leaves contain highly (B)[flammable / nonflammable] in oil. The extreme heat from the fire causes the shell to crack open. Finally, the seeds come out of the shell, hit the ground, and begin to grow. The fallen seeds are conveniently (C)[exposed / concealed] in the soft ash left over after the fire, which protects them from the harsh environment. Wildfire, often started by the parent tree, also burns practically everything on the ground, destroying other plants that would compete with the seeds for the water and sunlight needed for growth. As you can see, eucalyptus is only able to reproduce provided that there is fire.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 흐름상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: retain flammable exposed
release flammable concealed
release nonflammable concealed
retain nonflammable concealed
release flammable exposed
solution:
(A) 모체 식물에서 분리되는 경우를 말하고 있으므로, 일부 식물들은 극심한 경험을 견딘 뒤에서 씨앗을 ‘방출한다(release)'는 흐름이 자연스럽다.
retain 보유하다, 유지하다
(B) 유칼립투스 잎은 서로 마찰하면서 자연적으로 불이 붙을 정도이므로, 잎들이 아주 높은 ’flammable(가연성의, 인화성의)' 기름을 가졌다는 것이 흐름상 자연스럽다.
nonflammable 불연성의
(C) 가혹한 환경으로부터 그것을 보호한다는 내용이 이어지므로 화재 후에 남은 부드러운 재 속에 ‘concealed(감춰진)’이 흐름상 자연스럽다.
expose 노출하다

body:
Many plants opt to scatter their seeds by providing food to animals, but not all of them do. Some plants attach their seeds to passing animals, spreading them without any return benefit. Instead of tempting sweet fruits, these seeds are equipped with sharp hooks or needles. Devil’s claw stands out as the most vicious of these plants. Devil’s claw primarily inhabits the Kalahari Desert in South Africa, Namibia, and Botswana. Its blossoms (A)[resembling / resembled] pink trumpets eventually transform into fruits with many hooks. As these fruits dry, they become solid, and their hooks become tough enough to attach to the bodies of animals.
As animals pass by, the hooks extending in all directions will keep the dried fruit firmly attached to their fur. As the animals move away, the seeds from the fruit will be scattered in various locations. The attached hooks cause severe pain to the animals, making them (B)[feel / to feel] like the devil is scratching them with its horrifying claws. That is (C)[how / what] devil’s claw became known as the worst free rider.

윗글의 괄호 (A), (B), (C)에서 어법상 알맞은 말로 바르게 연결된 것은?
(A) (B) (C)
choices: resembling feel how
resembling to feel how
resembled to feel what
resembling feel what
resembled feel how
solution:
(A) 뒤에 문장의 동사 transform이 있으므로 앞의 명사구 Its blossoms를 수식하는 분사 자리이며, 수식받는 명사구가 ‘닮은’ 주체이자 resemble은 수동태를 만들 수 없는 동사이므로 능동을 나타내는 현재분사 resembling이 알맞다.
(B) 사역동사 make의 목적격보어로 동사원형 feel이 알맞다.
(C) 뒤에 완전한 절이 이어지므로 ‘~하는 방법’의 의미를 갖는 관계부사 how가 알맞다.

body:
Not all seeds are transported by animals. Some are carried by the wind. This approach is used by maple trees. Maple seeds are shaped like a boomerang with irregular ridges on the surface. When a maple seed falls from the tree, it spins around. This rotation makes the seed stay in the air longer and fly farther. It is similar to how helicopters get lifted and stay in the air using their propellers. The rotation caused by its wings allows the maple seed to elevate twice as high as non-rotating seeds. As a result, it can travel much farther from the parent tree. The rotation also slows down the speed of the fall, and the seed softly lands on the ground. This helps reduce the damage to the seed during the fall.

다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?
choices: Maple seeds rely on air currents, rather than animals, to move away from the parent tree.
A maple seed has a curved form and an uneven surface.
The spinning movement of maple seeds functions in a way similar to how a helicopter is lifted.
Seeds that spin reach about three times the height achieved by seeds that do not rotate.
Rotation reduces the downward speed of maple seeds, allowing them to reach the ground more gently.

body:
Where would you find the tallest tree in the world? You will have to visit Redwood National Park in the United States to find it. Redwoods are known as the tallest plants in the world. Typically, redwoods grow over 60 m, and it is easy ⓐto find them exceeding 90 m. Among them, a redwood named Hyperion stands enormously tall, reaching over 115 m. It holds the record as the world’s tallest tree. Before it was discovered, Helios, ⓑwhich was 114 m, was considered to be the tallest tree. However, in 2006, two naturalists found a tree taller than Helios. They were so overwhelmed by its height ⓒthat they named it after one of the Titans from Greek myths, Hyperion. Hyperion was the name of the Titan of the Sun, meaning “the highest one.” However, the odds of you ⓓseeing Hyperion at the park are slim to none. The park keeps its precise location a secret to protect it from potential harm caused by visitors. You may assume you can easily find it among the redwoods, but it is harder than you think. The height difference between Hyperion and its neighboring redwoods is merely a few meters, making ⓔthat nearly impossible to identify from the ground. Every redwood in the park will look like a giant from the bottom.

윗글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?
solution:
ⓔ that → it (뒤에 진목적어 to identify가 이어지므로, 'make+가목적어+목적격보어(형용사)+진목적어(to부정사)'의 구조로, that을 가목적어 it으로 고쳐야 한다.)
오답
ⓐ 가주어 it에 상응하는 진주어 역할을 하는 to부정사구 to find는 알맞다.
ⓒ ‘so ~ that+완전한 절(너무 ~해서 …하다)‘의 의미를 갖는 구문으로, 결과를 나타내는 완전한 절을 이끄는 접속사 that으로 알맞다.
ⓓ 전치사 of의 목적어 역할을 하는 동명사 seeing이며, you는 동명사의 의미상 주어로 알맞다.

body:
Plants will do anything to spread their seeds. They offer tasty food to animals in return for distributing their seeds. Jackfruit, the world’s largest tree fruit, has a sweet smell that attracts animals, similar to pineapples and bananas. It tempts animals to eat delicious fruit flesh, thereby getting them to eat the seeds. The fruit flesh is digested by the animals that consume it, but the seeds are not digested and pass through the animals’ digestive tracts untouched. When these animals poop out the seeds, the seeds begin to sprout and grow, and jackfruit spreads. In exchange for a satisfying meal, the animals spread the jackfruit seeds.

다음 글의 주제로 알맞은 것은?
choices: how jackfruit uses animals as a means to spread its seeds
the different digestion of fruit flesh and seeds by animals
various methods animals use to search for food in the wild
why jackfruit has a stronger scent than pineapples and bananas
the nutritional value of jackfruit compared to other tropical fruits
